title: Release Train Signal Hub & Lane Prioritization Matrix
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Objective: Create an operational 'Signal Hub' and a lane prioritization matrix that the Release Train can use to make deterministic go/no-go and staged roll decisions across runtime, console, and API surfaces. The Hub will consolidate signals (capacity, SLO risk, telemetry anomalies, critical customer launches, and regional resource constraints) into a single prioritized feed and recommended lane actions.

Scope:
- Define signal taxonomy and weightings (latency SLO drift, error budget burn, capacity headroom, pro-customer launches, compliance blackout windows).
- Prototype a lightweight dashboard (read-only) for launch owners showing lane state and recommended actions.
- Publish a prioritization matrix with explicit tie-breaking rules so PMs/eng/ops can agree on which cohort or lane gets precedence during contention.
- Define operational playbook for the on-call rotation and communications channel to surface urgent lane escalations.

Out of scope: automated gating (this ticket produces the feed & playbook; automation work will be follow-ups owned by ENG).

Acceptance criteria:
- Documented signal taxonomy with weightings and an example calculation walk-through.
- Draft prioritization matrix with at least 4 lane categories and tie-break rules reviewed by Eng and SRE.
- Dashboard prototype linked to current telemetry query endpoints (mocked data acceptable) and accessible to launch owners.
- On-call rotation template and escalation runbook published in Confluence.

Success metrics:
- Reduce time-to-decision in weekly release syncs by 30% (measured via meeting notes/time-to-resolution).
- Decrease last-minute cross-team capacity conflicts during launches by 40% in the following quarter (measured in launch postmortems).

Stakeholders:
- PM Owner: Ava Martinez
- Eng Lead: Priya Kaur (runtime)
- SRE/Capacity: Marcus Liu
- Console/Product Ops: Diego Ortega
- Design: Lila Nguyen (for dashboard mocks)

Risks & trade-offs:
- Over-weighting SLO signals could unduly delay strategic customer launches; matrix must include explicit override criteria for commercial-critical customers.
- A too-complex taxonomy will reduce adoption; initial version should be intentionally conservative and iterated after 2 launches.
- Tension between automation vs human-judgement: prioritize human-readable recommendations first, automation later.
